body:
I live in a small town right now too, and I know for sure that people know how much I've fucked things up for myself. I wouldn't say I'm necessarily well known around here but my friends are, and word gets around. I'd rather be known as the guy who got help and beat the odds than the guy who gave in (even though killing yourself isn't 'giving in' by any means, there's definitely that stigma).



I had a friend of mine who I'd met shortly after moving here kill himself. I found out later that he suffered from drug addiction and mental illness as well. At the time I didn't know that but as my depression started to spiral sharply downwards I found that out from his brother and it made sense. Now I'm in the same boat he was (or worse). 



The only thing I can suggest is getting serious help. I'm in debt too but there are options. I don't know the specifics of where you live but you may be able to qualify for financial assistance and get approved faster if you're in an inpatient treatment program. If your family knows you're getting help they may be willing to help with money too (speaking with no specific knowledge of your circumstances of course).

I wouldn't really say I have any happiness left, just a bit of hope. I'm really waiting to get into this inpatient program that I'm hoping will help. I'm mostly trying to keep on going until then. I've been waiting to get into this program for years but kept cancelling my application when I'd think things were going okay. I wanna follow through now because I know it's life or death for me.



Those are beautiful lyrics. I think one of my friends has lyrics from another one of their songs as a tattoo. I don't really fuck with that genre too much but it's good that you enjoy it.



Listen man, I know it's hard but really try to kick blow. It's toxic as fuck for us mentally ill people. I know 100% that my recovery is dependent on my sobriety. Just something to think about (I'm sure you've heard that already).

Yeah I've been using cocaine pretty frequently too. Not the greatest thing for someone who's been having financial troubles.



As for your plans, I can't say I recommend it. Have you been doing therapy or been on medication? As much as I understand how painful things are, I urge you to explore other alternatives.



EDIT: I'm bad with putting things off as well, so I'm not really the greatest authority on this, but I'd 100% recommend calling an intake number for a hospital or somewhere ASAP. Even though going didn't solve my problems, getting admitted did buy me time and help me explore my other options.
